strings.name: Lassina Zerbo
strings.role: Former prime minister of Burkina Faso; chairman of Rwanda Atomic Energy Board
strings.summary: Lassina Zerbo is a geophysicist and diplomat who led the Provisional Technical Secretariat of the CTBTO Preparatory Commission, advancing nuclear-monitoring data and international cooperation. He briefly served as Burkina Faso’s prime minister in 2021–2022 and continued working on peaceful nuclear technology in Africa and Rwanda’s energy policy.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 18 November 2026; the latest completed activity is documented in retrospective reporting on the 28 October Moscow meeting. Distinguish the Preparatory Commission from the organization envisaged after treaty entry into force, national from international offices, and nuclear cooperation agreements from operating projects.
strings.influence.rationale: Previously led the CTBTO Preparatory Commission, advancing international nuclear monitoring and disarmament diplomacy while also participating in national governance.
strings.facts.f1.label: Birth and scientific training
strings.facts.f1.value: Born on 10 October 1963, he is a Burkinabé national with a doctorate in geophysics from France’s Université Paris XI. He worked in mineral exploration at BHP Minerals and Anglo American before applying his geophysical-monitoring experience to international nuclear-test verification.
strings.facts.f2.label: Public roles across countries
strings.facts.f2.value: He was executive secretary of the CTBTO Preparatory Commission in 2013–2021 and prime minister of Burkina Faso from December 2021 to January 2022. He subsequently continued as chairman of Rwanda Atomic Energy Board and became Rwanda’s presidential energy adviser. The board chairmanship is separate from the agency’s chief executive position.
strings.highlights.h1.title: Connecting monitoring science and diplomacy
strings.highlights.h1.text: He promoted monitoring data for research, tsunami warning and nuclear-test analysis, alongside science diplomacy with member states. Nature’s 2017 annual personalities feature covered his response to North Korean nuclear tests. Advances in monitoring do not mean that the Comprehensive Nuclear-Test-Ban Treaty has entered into force.
strings.highlights.h2.title: Peaceful nuclear energy and the prerequisites for development
strings.highlights.h2.text: Working on Rwanda’s nuclear cooperation, he emphasizes training engineers and regulators and regional collaboration. Cooperation with Russia in 2026 included a small modular reactor roadmap. Adding nuclear power to the energy mix is a policy goal for the early 2030s; agreements do not establish that reactors have been built or entered service.
strings.timeline.t1.title: Moderated a discussion on nuclear technology in Africa
strings.timeline.t1.text: He moderated a nuclear-technology session during the business programme of the third Russia–Africa Summit in Moscow, covering workforce development, nuclear infrastructure and regional cooperation. A 1 November retrospective confirmed his participation; assessments of Africa’s nuclear prospects remain the speakers’ views.
strings.timeline.t2.title: Co-chaired Rwanda–Russia nuclear coordination meeting
strings.timeline.t2.text: He co-chaired the first Joint Coordinating Committee meeting with a senior Rosatom executive, and the parties signed a small modular reactor cooperation roadmap. A 30 June release and 1 July report support that the meeting had occurred in June. Cooperation also covered nuclear science, workforce training and regulatory preparation.
strings.timeline.t3.title: Became Rwanda’s presidential energy adviser
strings.timeline.t3.text: He was appointed energy adviser and a member of the Strategy and Policy Council in the Office of the President. Presidential Order 071/01, published on 28 August, gives the appointment effect from 22 May. This advisory appointment is separate from his earlier chairmanship of Rwanda Atomic Energy Board.
strings.timeline.t4.title: Coup ended his premiership
strings.timeline.t4.text: The military overthrew President Kaboré and announced the dissolution of the government and National Assembly, ending Zerbo’s brief premiership. Deteriorating security was among the military’s stated reasons; this was not an electoral transfer of government.
strings.timeline.t5.title: Parliament backed his policy programme
strings.timeline.t5.text: He presented four priorities to the National Assembly: restoring security, helping displaced people return home, national reconciliation and fighting corruption. There were 103 votes in favour, 24 abstentions and none against. Parliamentary backing followed his appointment; the policies were goals rather than demonstrated achievements.
strings.timeline.t6.title: Appointed prime minister of Burkina Faso
strings.timeline.t6.text: President Roch Marc Christian Kaboré appointed him to replace Christophe Dabiré. A new cabinet was formed on 13 December, prioritizing security and restoration of state governance amid continuing armed conflict and public discontent.
strings.timeline.t7.title: Became the CTBTO’s third executive secretary
strings.timeline.t7.text: Succeeding Tibor Tóth, he led the Preparatory Commission’s Provisional Technical Secretariat and promoted the monitoring system and nuclear-test-ban diplomacy. His tenure ended on 31 July 2021, with Robert Floyd taking over the next day. This was not the office of United Nations secretary-general.
strings.timeline.t8.title: Moved into international nuclear-test monitoring
strings.timeline.t8.text: He moved from mining geophysics to the CTBTO as director of the International Data Centre, serving until 2013. His work covered monitoring-data processing, technical support to member states and scientific exchange, laying the groundwork for his later leadership of the Secretariat.
